summary: Introduces a Schatten-norm optimizer family that unifies SGD and Muon-like matrix updates with dimension-free stationarity theory; it is adjacent because the contribution is a broader optimizer framework, not a Muon variant.
source_title: Schattor: Schatten-family methods for deep learning optimization

summary: Analyzes which Schatten-p geometries are optimal under different scaling/noise regimes, explaining when Muon-like Schatten-infinity updates help and when smaller-p geometries are preferable.
source_title: When to use what Schatten-$p$ norm in deep learning?

summary: Combines zeroth-order fine-tuning with parameter-free LMO methods to reduce memory and tuning burden, borrowing Muon-style geometry but focusing on ZO/PF optimization broadly.
source_title: Zero-order Parameter-free Optimization for LMO-based Methods: Novel Approach for Efficient Fine-tuning

summary: Diagnoses coordinate-scale heterogeneity in matrices before Newton-Schulz, then proposes coordinate-adaptive dual whitening; Muon appears mainly as a matrix-aware baseline and motivation.
source_title: Zeta: Dual Whitening for Matrix Optimization via Coordinate-Adaptive Preconditioning

summary: Tests module-wise manifold assignments for GPT-2 training, finding Stiefel constraints suit attention while DGram suits MLPs; Muon is used through a Manifold Muon lens rather than modified directly.
source_title: Different Layers, Different Manifolds: Module-Wise Weight-Space Geometry in Transformer Optimization

paper: Overcoming Rank Collapse in Feedback Alignment
summary: Studies why feedback alignment fails in deeper networks and uses orthogonalized/Muon-style updates to increase feedback-signal rank, but the target is biologically plausible learning, not optimizer design.
source_title: Overcoming Rank Collapse in Feedback Alignment

summary: Adds a polynomial weight-preconditioning layer that reshapes singular spectra during LLM pretraining and can be merged away at inference; Muon is one optimizer tested with the architectural preconditioner.
source_title: PC Layer: Polynomial Weight Preconditioning for Improving LLM Pre-Training

summary: Optimizes for rollout/test-time performance under feedback mismatch rather than validation loss, treating Muon as one possible gradient-wise preconditioner inside a broader DoPr framework.
source_title: Double Preconditioning (DoPr): Optimization for Test-Time Performance, not Validation Loss

summary: Presents a real-time vision model family with NMS-free heads and training changes; Muon-SGD appears as part of the recipe, but the main contribution is architecture/system design.
source_title: Ultralytics YOLO26: Unified Real-Time End-to-End Vision Models

summary: Builds event-grounded world-action-model pretraining for VLA/video-action learning; Muon is part of the large-scale training stack rather than the object of study.
source_title: WALL-WM: Carving World Action Modeling at the Event Joints

paper: Exploiting Weight-Space Symmetries for Approximating Curvature
summary: Uses weight-space symmetry averaging to construct tractable curvature approximations from single gradients, recovering Shampoo/Muon-like structures as cases of a broader symmetry framework.
source_title: Exploiting weight-space symmetries for approximating curvature

summary: Reports a 12B MoE code/general model and mentions Muon in the FP8 hybrid-precision training recipe; it is model-report evidence of Muon use, not an optimizer contribution.
source_title: Mellum2 Technical Report

paper: On the Optimizer Dependence of Neural Scaling Laws
summary: Shows scaling-law exponents vary with optimizer choice in random-feature regression and related settings, using Matrix-Sign/Muon-like methods as one optimizer family under comparison.
source_title: On the Optimizer Dependence of Neural Scaling Laws

summary: Introduces parameterized local linear attention for language modeling and uses Muon to stabilize/scale training; the optimizer is enabling infrastructure, not the paper's main method.
source_title: Parallax: Parameterized Local Linear Attention for Language Modeling

paper: How the Optimizer Shapes Learned Solutions in Equivariant Neural Networks
summary: Compares Adam and Muon across equivariant/geometric models, finding Muon often improves optimization; it analyzes optimizer effects rather than proposing a new optimizer.
source_title: How the Optimizer Shapes Learned Solutions in Equivariant Neural Networks

summary: Identifies early stabilization of trace-normalized singular spectra during LLM pretraining across schedules and optimizers including Muon, connecting spectral dynamics to two-phase loss curves.
source_title: The Stability of Singular Distribution: A Spectral Perspective on the Two-Phase Dynamics of Language Model Pre-training

summary: Interprets Transformer residual updates as optimizer steps and designs architectures inspired by momentum, Adam, Muon, and SOAP; the contribution is architectural, not an optimizer update rule.
source_title: Momentum Streams for Optimizer-Inspired Transformers

summary: Measures FFN representation spectra and shows AdamW and Muon produce different spectral scaling laws at fixed architecture, framing optimizer choice as a capacity-scaling axis.
source_title: Same Architecture, Different Capacity: Optimizer-Induced Spectral Scaling Laws

summary: Develops theory for scale-invariant optimizers under norm geometry and heavy-tailed noise, including Muon and Scion as examples within a broader optimization principle.
source_title: Scale-Invariant Neural Network Optimization: Norm Geometry and Heavy-Tailed Noise

summary: Surveys LLM optimizer design from AdamW through memory-efficient and matrix-based methods, positioning Muon within the broader optimizer landscape rather than introducing a method.
source_title: Navigating LLM Valley: From AdamW to Memory-Efficient and Matrix-Based Optimizers

summary: Shows full fine-tuning with the same optimizer used in pretraining can reduce forgetting, comparing Muon and AdamW behavior as evidence for optimizer-shaped model states.
source_title: Optimizer-Model Consistency: Full Finetuning with the Same Optimizer as Pretraining Forgets Less

paper: Benchmarking Optimizers for MLPs in Tabular Deep Learning
summary: Benchmarks 15 optimizers for tabular MLPs and finds Muon strong against AdamW; it is empirical optimizer evaluation rather than new algorithm design.
source_title: Benchmarking Optimizers for MLPs in Tabular Deep Learning

summary: Tests normalization-layer choices with AdamW and Muon at 1B scale, showing Dynamic Erf interacts badly with Muon while RMSNorm/DyT behave differently.
source_title: Does Your Optimizer Care How You Normalize? Normalization-Optimizer Coupling in LLM Training

summary: Uses rolling-window spectra of parameter updates to analyze phase transitions such as grokking and loss plateaus; optimizer spectra are diagnostic tools, not new update rules.
source_title: Spectral Edge Dynamics: An Analytical-Empirical Study of Phase Transitions in Neural Network Training

summary: Improves FSDP/ZeRO infrastructure for block-structured computations and non-element-wise optimizers such as Shampoo and Muon, focusing on sharding/runtime support.
source_title: veScale-FSDP: Flexible and High-Performance FSDP at Scale

summary: Studies Chinchilla-style and optimizer-specific scaling laws across AdamW, Muon, Shampoo, SOAP, and others, asking how optimizer choice changes compute/data/model scaling.
source_title: Towards Robust Scaling Laws for Optimizers

paper: Data Distribution as an Optimizer Lever
summary: Analyzes whether changing training data distribution can steer optimizer generalization behavior, comparing GD and SAM; it is adjacent to optimizer choice but not Muon-specific.
source_title: Data Distribution as a Lever for Guiding Optimizers Toward Superior Generalization in LLMs

summary: Combines GPTQ quantization, LoRA, distillation, and Muon-based fine-tuning in a deployment pipeline for compressed LLMs, using Muon as a component rather than proposing it.
source_title: Advancing Model Refinement: Muon-Optimized Distillation and Quantization for LLM Deployment

summary: Adds learnable scalar multipliers to matrix layers to escape weight-decay/noise equilibrium norms, validating the scaling idea under Adam and Muon.
source_title: Learnable Multipliers: Freeing the Scale of Language Model Matrix Layers

summary: Argues vanilla MLP INRs fail at high frequencies due to stable-rank degradation and uses Muon-like high-rank updates/rank regularization to preserve representation rank.
source_title: Optimizing Rank for High-Fidelity Implicit Neural Representations
